channel.title: Usama Arshad, Writing
channel.description: Offensive security writing: CTF writeups, vulnerability research, and exploitation technique.

item.title: Fifteen challenges, fourteen flags: BlackHat MEA 2026 CTF qualifiers
item.description: Full writeups for all 15 qualifier challenges: an 8-query Prony attack on a secret modulus, an RSA oracle leaking only popcount, a real io_uring double-free driven to root, eBPF-decrypted licence shellcode, a CSS selector oracle under a JS-free CSP, and an ffmpeg external-data-reference file read.

item.title: Fifty-nine CVEs in one year: what WordPress plugins keep getting wrong
item.description: A data-backed study of 51 catalogued WordPress plugin CVEs across 46 plugins: 53% unauthenticated, 49% data disclosure, and one recurring root cause behind nearly all of it.

item.title: Your allowlist is inside the attacker's process
item.description: Loopback binds, IP allowlists and VPC boundaries all fail the same way: they check where a request came from, when the attacker is already there.

item.title: The AI assistant kept a diary
item.description: Local LLM prompt histories are a new DFIR artifact class: plaintext, timestamped records of intent, and often the passphrase.
